spec.description: Satisfactory Factories planner usage. Server-derived room and account gauges, plus an anonymous browser heartbeat that counts local plans and signed-out users the server cannot see. Every query is pinned to job="satisfactory-factories-preview"; production and preview export the same metric names.

spec.title: Active Browsers
spec.description: Browsers that sent a heartbeat in the last 15 minutes. Counts local-only and signed-out users, who are invisible to the server otherwise.

spec.title: Signed In vs Signed Out
spec.description: Whether somebody is signed in. Never who.

spec.title: Live Sockets
spec.description: Open realtime connections. One socket carries every synced tab in a browser, so this is below the active-browser count by design.

spec.title: Signed-in Share
spec.description: What fraction of active browsers have an account signed in.

spec.title: Database Readable
spec.description: 1 when the last scrape read Mongo. At 0 the room and account gauges are frozen at their last values, not actually zero. This is the one to alert on.

spec.title: Active Browsers Over Time
spec.description: Stacked, so the total height is every active browser.

spec.title: Live Sockets Over Time
spec.description: Realtime connections held open.

spec.title: Records
spec.description: Now, and the 24 hour average and peak. Built from subqueries over the scrape series.

spec.title: Plans Open in Browsers
spec.description: Planner tabs, not browser tabs. Local plans never reach the server, so this is the only place they are counted.

spec.title: Cloud Share of Plans
spec.description: What fraction of open plans are synced rather than local only. The headline adoption number for syncing.

spec.title: Factories in Browsers
spec.description: Factories summed across active browsers, local plans included.

spec.title: Plans per Browser
spec.description: Average planner tabs open per active browser.

spec.title: Factories per Browser
spec.description: Average factories per active browser. The rough answer to how big a plan people actually build.

spec.title: Plans Over Time, Local vs Cloud
spec.description: Stacked. The cloud band growing against the local band is sync adoption.

spec.title: Factories in Browsers Over Time
spec.description: Total factories across active browsers.

spec.title: Registered Accounts
spec.description: Rows in the users collection.

spec.title: Synced Plans
spec.description: Live rooms on the server, tombstoned ones excluded.

spec.title: Shared Plans
spec.description: Synced plans that have an invite link allocated.

spec.title: Share Rate
spec.description: What fraction of synced plans have been shared with somebody.

spec.title: Plan Access
spec.description: One row per person-to-plan link. Creating a plan gives you one; joining somebody's shared plan gives you another. So this is plans plus extra people on them.

spec.title: Collaborators
spec.description: People editing plans they do not own: access grants minus plans. This is the number that says whether sharing is actually being used, rather than just available.

spec.title: Factories per Synced Plan
spec.description: sf_room_factories_total / sf_rooms_total.

spec.title: Synced Plans Over Time
spec.description: Stacked by whether the plan has an invite link.

spec.title: Accounts and Access Over Time
spec.description: All three grow in normal use. Access falling without accounts falling is the sweeper clearing deleted plans.

spec.title: Edits, All Time
spec.description: Accepted edits summed across live plans. Falls when a plan is deleted, because those edits no longer exist; that is why it is a gauge rather than a counter.

spec.title: Edits, Last 24h
spec.description: Edits added since the low point of the last 24 hours. Measured from the trough rather than from the value 24h ago, so it answers from the first scrape instead of reading No data for a day, and cannot go negative when a plan is deleted.

spec.title: Edits Over Time
spec.description: The cumulative line. The strongest single indicator of whether the planner is being used.

spec.title: Edits per 24h, Over Time
spec.description: Rolling 24-hour edit count. Any window works by changing the range in the query.

spec.title: Active Accounts
spec.description: Accounts whose last accepted edit falls inside each window. Signing in, creating a plan and joining one are not edits and do not count.

spec.title: Active Accounts Over Time
spec.description: The windows plotted together. The 30-day line is thin for the first month after release: it is seeded from an activity log that is trimmed per plan, so early history is partial.

spec.title: Stickiness
spec.description: Accounts active in a day against those active in a month. High means people come back; low means they visit once.

spec.title: Faults, Last 24h
spec.description: Every counted fault in the last day, client and server together. Indicative rather than authoritative: the client half arrives over an unauthenticated endpoint.

spec.title: Server Errors, Last 24h
spec.description: HTTP 5xx responses. The line that matters most, because a 500 means the server itself failed rather than refusing something.

spec.title: Plan Repairs, Last 24h
spec.description: Loaded plans that had to be corrected before they could be used. Each one is a plan that was saved wrong at some point.

spec.title: Faults by Reason, Last 24h
spec.description: Every reason with at least one occurrence in the last day, largest first. A reason at zero is absent from this panel by design; that is the good news.

spec.title: Faults Over Time
spec.description: A rolling one-hour count per reason. An hour rather than a five-minute rate because faults are rare: at five minutes a single one is a pixel-wide blip on a day-long axis and you would never see it.

spec.title: Client and Server
spec.description: Which half of the app is reporting. A spike on one side only usually says where to look first.

spec.title: HTTP Errors by Status
spec.description: Per-response view. 4xx is dominated by ordinary refusals and is mostly noise; 5xx is not.

spec.title: Records Lost After a Commit
spec.description: Times somebody's change was saved and the record of it was not. Each one is a silent gap in the activity log or the account stamps.

spec.title: New Accounts
spec.description: Registrations inside each rolling window. Read from the registration date accounts have always carried, so it is exact and correct all the way back, not just since this metric shipped.

spec.title: New Accounts This Week
spec.description: Registrations in the last 7 days.

spec.title: New Accounts This Month
spec.description: Registrations in the last 30 days.

spec.title: New Accounts Over Time
spec.description: Each rolling window plotted. A step up in the 24h line is a signup; the wider lines are the trend.

spec.title: Sign-ins
spec.description: Accounts that signed in inside each window. Separate from editing: signing in, reading a plan and changing nothing is a real thing people do.

spec.title: Sign-ins, All Time
spec.description: Sign-ins summed across accounts. Approximate: the count is written after the token is issued and is allowed to fail, and it counts from release rather than being backfilled.

spec.title: Sign-ins Over Time
spec.description: Rolling sign-in windows. Compare against Active Accounts: a gap means people are signing in and not building.

spec.title: Of Those Who Signed In, How Many Edited
spec.description: Active accounts over signed-in accounts, both on 7 days. Low means people arrive and do not build.

spec.title: Share Links Created
spec.description: Snapshot links that exist, all time. Counted from the rows themselves, so it is exact and complete, and falls only if a row is deleted by hand.

spec.title: Share Links Opened
spec.description: Opens summed across every link. Counted when the link is fetched, which is the same moment the planner adds the plan as a tab.

spec.title: Opens per Link
spec.description: Average opens per link. Around 1 means links are made and read once; well above means they are being passed around.

spec.title: New Share Links
spec.description: Links created inside each rolling window. Read from the creation date the rows have always carried, so it is correct all the way back, not just since this metric shipped.

spec.title: Share Links Created Over Time
spec.description: Each rolling window plotted. A step up in the 24h line is somebody making a link.

spec.title: Most Opened Share Links
spec.description: The links people actually pass around. Top 20 only, and a link that has never been opened is left out rather than shown at zero.

spec.title: Biggest Plans
spec.description: The largest synced plans by factory count, with the account that owns each. Top 20 only.

spec.title: Busiest Accounts
spec.description: Accepted edits per account. Approximate by design: the count is written after the edit commits and is allowed to fail, and it starts from zero at release rather than being backfilled. Top 20 only.

spec.title: Accounts With the Most Factories
spec.description: Factories summed over the synced plans each account created. Top 20 only.

spec.title: Largest Plan
spec.description: Factory count of the biggest single synced plan.

spec.title: Browsers by Build
spec.description: Active browsers by the build they are running. Anything the version pattern does not recognise counts under "other".

spec.title: Build Adoption Over Time
spec.description: Stacked. After a release, watch the old band drain. While it is still wide, a breaking change will hurt.

spec.title: Browsers by Commit
spec.description: Active browsers by the commit their bundle was built from. A build that reported no commit, such as a local one, counts under "unknown". Capped to the busiest 25 commits.

spec.title: Commit Rollout Over Time
spec.description: Stacked. After a deploy, watch the previous commit drain. This is the panel that says whether a rollout has actually reached people, which a version number cannot: several commits ship under one version.

spec.title: Browsers on an Unknown Commit
spec.description: Builds reporting no usable commit. Expect this to be non-zero only for local development builds.

spec.title: On an Unrecognised Build
spec.description: Browsers reporting a version the label pattern refused. Expect zero. Anything sustained means either a bad build string or somebody poking the endpoint.

spec.title: 👥 Live Right Now · from browsers, 15 min window
